Define, import, and export report profiles

Source: R/profiles.R
reportProfile.Rd

A report profile is an ordered selection of modules used to produce an ecological report and a data-status report. The ecological module pool is the collection of YAML files in reportSections; the data-status module pool is the separate collection in statusSections. These are libraries of available modules, not lists of sections that must all be rendered. A profile selects an ordered subset of either library. For example, "report::introduction" selects an ecological module, whereas "status::spatial" selects a data-status module, including when it is used in an ecological report's appendix. These prefixes select module libraries; they are not R namespace calls.

Usage

reportProfile(
  name,
  report = character(),
  status = character(),
  description = ""
)

read_profile(file)

write_profile(profile, file, overwrite = FALSE, object = NULL)

profile_names(object = NULL)

add_profile(object, profile, overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

name

A non-empty profile name.

report

An ordered set of modules for report().

status

An ordered set of modules for status().

description

Optional descriptive text.

file

Path to a profile YAML file.

profile

A reportProfile object, a profile name registered in object, or a bundled profile name. write_profile() accepts either an object or a name.

overwrite

A logical value controlling whether an existing profile or file can be replaced.

object

A camReport object.

Value

reportProfile() and read_profile() return a reportProfile object. profile_names() returns a character vector. add_profile() invisibly returns the modified camReport object, and write_profile() invisibly returns the output path.

Details

Profile entries may be character vectors or data frames. Character entries use "source::module" notation; unqualified entries default to the report pool for report and the status pool for status. A data frame can also contain a parent column to override the parent declared by a module. This makes it possible, for example, to place status modules below an ecological report's appendix without modifying the shared module YAML files.

Bundled profiles are registered in each object created by camData(). User profiles can be registered with add_profile() and shared as YAML files with read_profile() and write_profile(). See the report-profile guide for a reusable custom profile and cross-library appendix example.

See also

sections(), section_names(), report(), status()

Examples

profile <- reportProfile(
  name = "brief",
  report = c("introduction", "results"),
  status = c("abstract", "availability")
)
profile
#> Report profile: brief
#>   ecological report modules: 2
#>   data-status modules: 2

profile_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
write_profile(profile, profile_file)
identical(read_profile(profile_file), profile)
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(profile_file)
